correctness.rationale: The normalized I_{1/2}, I_{3/2} functions reduce the quotient to F/G. Derivative ratio D=G′/F′ has derivative L′(q−γ), where q=0.5(log U)′ for U=(sinh²x−x²)/x⁴, a positive nondegenerate symmetric-moment generating function. Thus q strictly rises from 0 to 1, giving one minimum of D; P=FD−G has P′=FD′, crosses zero only once, and F/G has one global maximum. Exact endpoint series and a stationary equation yield the small-tilt and double-logarithmic critical laws. The checker validates 742 supplementary identities and comparisons but the all-parameter assertions rest on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The parameter-sharp constant governs a natural inequality for the positive-power modified Bessel moment and refines explicit published sufficient constants. Its unique equality point provides full optimality at every tilt; the near-critical law displays a non-obvious boundary-layer location involving log(1/δ)+2loglog(1/δ), plus an additive constant surplus of order 1/log(1/δ). These are structural analytic conclusions and a natural continuous-parameter classification, not arbitrary numerical examples.
